source.text: ወናሁ፡ *መጽአ፡ በትእልፊተ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ከመ፡ ይግበር፡ ፍትሐ፡ †ላዕሌሆሙ፡† ወይሕጕሎሙ፡ ለረሲዓን፡ ወ*ይዘልፍ፡ ኵሎ፡ ዘሥጋ፡ በእንተ፡ ኵሉ፡ *ዘገብሩ፡ ወረስዑ፡ ላዕሌሁ፡ ኃጥኣን፡ [ወ]ረሲዓን።
source.note: Low-confidence critical rendering of the selected Charles 1906 print, p. 4/PDF42. The printed daggered judgment expression and adopted emendation are retained; apparatus conjectures are not silently substituted. The English discloses uncertain antecedent and clause attachment. No new manuscript collation or publication approval.

transcription_uncertainties.issue: The daggered judgment phrase is read provisionally as “upon them”; its antecedent remains uncertain.
Selected final action/relative construction corrupt or defective; no silent Greek/Jude completion.
Plural multitude/myriad expression; not an asserted exact headcount of ten thousand.

translation.text: Look, he comes with myriads of holy ones[a] to carry out judgment upon them,[b] to destroy the godless, and to reprove all flesh for all they did—and they acted impiously against him, sinners [and] godless ones.[c]

footnotes.text: The selected text has no explicit “his” with the holy ones. “Myriads” does not assert an exact headcount.

“Upon them” renders the provisional reading of the printed, daggered expression, checked against the same-page form in 1:8. The antecedent is unresolved. Charles’s note 20 proposes a different reading, supported in sense by the Greek; it is not substituted here.

The dash presents a trial reading of the abrupt sequence, not punctuation supplied by the print. It leaves the named groups at the end, preserves the finite impiety verb, and does not add a second “for.” The English “they” reflects the working plural verb reading without settling how the final nouns relate to it or how the two actions are linked. The impiety verb is Charles’s emendation already printed in the verse body, as disclosed in note 25. The additional clause proposed in that same note is not printed in the body and is not supplied here.
